title: Add Origin-Anchored Project Key and adaptive handshake to stabilize streamed tool-calls and OpenAI-compat mapping
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduce a new Origin-Anchored-Project-Key header to reduce replay across origins, an adaptive handshake that falls back to signed-nonce when streaming preflight fails, and OpenAI-compat header mapping for legacy Authorization semantics.
description:
Motivation: Streaming tool/function calls (toolcalls) are sensitive to cross-origin conditions and long-lived browser streams can be interrupted by conservative intermediaries. We need a pragmatic auth/headermap that: (1) reduces accidental token replay between origins, (2) keeps browser streaming stable under CORS-restrictive proxies, and (3) preserves compatibility with our OpenAI-compat surface.

Summary of changes: - Introduce a new optional header 'Origin-Anchored-Project-Key' (OA-PK) that encodes a project-scoped key bound to the request Origin; when present, runtime validates the header and refuses cross-origin reuse unless the signature includes the target origin. - Add an adaptive streaming handshake: servers attempt a lightweight preflight using the Prefetch-Nonce header; if the preflight fails (CORS or network error), the client and server fall back to a signed-session nonce exchange using X-Rdwd-Signed-Nonce to resume streaming toolcalls without exposing long-lived tokens in the stream. - Provide an OpenAI-compat mapping layer: incoming 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' from legacy clients will be normalized into either OA-PK or scoped project tokens depending on token prefix and claims; we document the heuristics and deprecation timeline (90 days). - Small surface and SDK changes: TypeScript SDK adds a helper to generate OA-PK for browser usages, Python SDK exposes a helper to detect preflight failures and switch handshake modes. - Observability: add metrics for handshake type (prefetch_success/prefetch_fallback), origin_mismatch_rejects, and token_mapping_rates.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked: ENG-2319 - [x] Server runtime validation for OA-PK - [x] Adaptive handshake implemented in streaming proxy - [x] OpenAI-compat header mapping implemented - [x] TS/PY SDK helpers - [x] Unit and integration tests for handshake fallbacks - [x] Docs/upgrade notes added

Commits (high level): - 9a1b2c: wire up OA-PK header parsing and signature verification in streaming ingress - 5f3ee1: implement preflight-prefetch path and metrics - 2b7d5a: add signed-nonce fallback and X-Rdwd-Signed-Nonce marshaling - c4d08f: add openai-compat normalization layer and tests - d15a2b: SDK helpers + examples + docs updates

Changed files (high level): - runtime/streaming/handshake.go: core adaptive handshake and OA-PK verifier - runtime/auth/mapping.go: openai-compat normalization and token classifier - api/docs/upgrade-auth.md: new header docs and deprecation timeline - sdk/ts/src/streaming/helpers.ts: OA-PK generator + preflight helper - sdk/python/redwood/streaming/handshake.py: fallback helper - observability/metrics_registry.yaml: new metrics - tests/integration/streaming-handshake.test.ts

Runtime behavior notes: - OA-PK is optional; if not provided we fall back to existing scoped tokens. - OA-PK payload is HMAC(project_key_id || origin || timestamp) with a short TTL (2 minutes) to limit replay risk. Servers reject OA-PK if origin in signature does not match the observed Origin header. - Prefetch-Nonce: client sends Prefetch-Nonce: <opaque> in an OPTIONS-like preflight over the same connection; if server returns 200 + Prefetch-Allowed hint, client proceeds with stream. If preflight errors or times out, client restarts stream using X-Rdwd-Signed-Nonce signed by its short-lived keypair (sdk helper produces this). - OpenAI-compat mapping: tokens beginning with 'rdw_' are mapped to project tokens; tokens starting 'oa_legacy' are treated as compatibility-only and will be rejected after the deprecation window.

Review conversation (selected): - Omar Singh (reviewer) 2026-02-19: "Can we make OA-PK tolerant of subdomain variations for customers who use dynamic host routing? Rejecting strictly on exact origin may break some corporate setups." - Maya Chen (author) 2026-02-19: "Good point. I've added a project-configurable origin-allowlist with optional wildcard support; the default remains strict. See runtime/config.go changes (commit 9a1b2c)." - Luis Alvarez (reviewer) 2026-02-20: "Concern: doubling handshake paths increases attack surface. What are the telemetry signals to detect misuse?" - Maya Chen 2026-02-20: "Added metrics origin_mismatch_rejects and handshake_fallback_rate; we also emit an audit log when OA-PK signature fails so security can investigate. See observability changes." - Asha Patel (reviewer) 2026-02-21: "SDK ergonomics look good; can we add a small example for Next.js streaming?" - Maya Chen 2026-02-22: "Added an example in sdk/ts/examples/nextjs-prefetch.md and linked from docs."

CI summary: - unit-tests: pass - integration-tests (streaming): flaky on first run (timeout in CI env), rerun passed - linters: pass - performance-canary: minor regression in microbenchmark (0.9% p50 increase) traced to extra signature verification; added a hotfix to avoid double-parsing headers which removed regression.

Backward compatibility and migration: - Legacy clients that send Authorization: Bearer <token> continue to work; the compatibility layer will prefer OA-PK if present. - We add a 90-day deprecation for legacy oa_legacy tokens; banner and console notice will be shown to admins. - Admins can opt-in to permissive origin wildcards during a migration window.

Security review: - Security reviewed the OA-PK wire format and recommended the short TTL and inclusion of origin in the HMAC. - We also added a step to rotate short-lived project keys periodically and record rotation events in audit logs.

Documentation & rollout: - api/docs/upgrade-auth.md describes the new headers, handshake flow diagrams, and SDK examples. - Console shows a one-time banner for customers using legacy tokens. - Rollout plan: feature-flagged on main for 2 weeks, enable gradual rollout to hosted API, then ship Dedicated config flags for origin allowlists.

Follow-ups / TODOs: - ENG-2334: add a central migration dashboard showing handshake_fallback_rate by project - Improve binary size of TS helper (remove crypto polyfill) - Consider an eventual signed JWT variant for OA-PK to interoperate with some IdP flows

Merge outcome: Squash-merged to main 2026-02-25 after addressing linter comments and stabilizing flaky integration test.
